findings.title: prisma is used without being imported
findings.body: getClient calls prisma.credential.update(...) at line 96, but this file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma; the PR only added the z and parseRefreshTokenResponse imports. The package will not type-check/build, so Salesforce calendar and this credential-sync path are unusable.

findings.title: Google credential key is replaced with the SafeParse result object
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the result of safeParse ({ success, data }), not the parsed token data. Assigning that object to key and writing it to credential.key means the stored Google credential no longer matches googleCredentialSchema. The next construction/refresh of this credential will fail schema parsing, breaking Google Calendar for the user. Store parsed.data (or change the helper to return data) instead.

findings.title: Sync-mode refresh returns a raw fetch Response to callers expecting app-specific token objects
findings.body: When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the native Response from the parent endpoint. Several callers treat the return value as their provider client's response: Google reads res.data, HubSpot reads expiresIn/accessToken directly, and ZohoBigin/ZohoCRM read tokenInfo.data. Those values are undefined, so the code writes empty/undefined credentials to the DB and subsequent API calls fail. The helper needs to parse the response and return the shape each caller expects, or the callers must handle the fetch Response explicitly.

findings.title: Sync-mode token schema does not pass through provider token fields and fabricates a refresh token
findings.body: [z.string().toString()] evaluates to the literal key '[object Object]' (and the second computed key overwrites the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema only validates access_token and strips all other fields because z.object is not passthrough. The code then invents refresh_token: 'refresh_token' when it is absent (lines 25-27). In sync mode this drops expires_in/refresh_token/scope/instance_url from responses and overwrites real refresh tokens with that dummy value in callers such as Office365 and Zoom, causing repeated refreshes and eventual broken credentials. Use a passthrough schema and preserve existing refresh tokens.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID during sync refresh
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is userId, but this caller passes credentialId (the credential row ID). With credential sync enabled, the parent endpoint receives a calcomUserId that is actually a credential ID, so it will look up/return tokens for the wrong user or fail. The method should receive and pass credential.userId.

findings.title: Zoom sync refresh uses the folder name zoomvideo instead of the app slug zoom
findings.body: The rest of the Zoom app identifies itself with appId/slug 'zoom' (e.g. the callback creates appId: 'zoom' and the install path uses slug zoom), and the credential webhook looks up apps by their canonical DB slug. Passing 'zoomvideo' to the parent sync endpoint makes it inconsistent with those identifiers, so the parent cannot reliably resolve the app and token sync fails.

findings.title: Salesforce connection uses the old access token after refreshing
findings.body: getClient fetches and persists a new access_token at lines 96-99, but the returned jsforce.Connection is still created with credentialKey.access_token, the value loaded before the refresh. If the old token is expired, the new connection is immediately unusable; the freshly parsed token should be used.

findings.title: Malformed webhook bodies and invalid ciphertext return 500 instead of 4xx
findings.body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws a ZodError for invalid payloads, and symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse at lines 57-59 can throw for bad ciphertext or invalid JSON. There is no try/catch, so Next returns a 500 to the caller. Webhook senders will treat malformed requests as server failures and retry them; validate and return 400.
